validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE check. Real, completed FGT capacity project, independently confirmed by TWO federal-government origins that reference the SAME docket number (cross-checked, not just the same name): (1) the Federal Register notice of FGT's prior-notice filing (govinfo.gov FR-2018-11-15, documents 2018-24882/2018-24887 -- two identical Combined-Notice-of-Filings publications of the same text): 'Take notice that on November 1, 2018, Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (FGT)...filed in Docket No. CP19-12-000 a prior notice request pursuant to...FGT's blanket certificate issued in Docket No. CP82-553-000 for authorization of the East Louisiana Project. FGT proposes to construct/modify, own, and operate certain natural gas mainline facilities and appurtenances at an existing compressor station site in Perry County, Mississippi. In addition, FGT proposes to install a new regulator, valves, Electronic Flow Meter and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, and appurtenances, in FGT's permanent right-of-way easement at an existing mainline valve site in Washington Parish, Louisiana. This project will allow FGT to provide additional capacity of up to 75 million cubic feet per day of available firm transportation service to Entergy Louisiana, LLC in Washington Parish, Louisiana.' (2) EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' historical-projects workbook (independent US government compilation, different agency/process from FERC) carries a matching row: Project Name 'East Louisiana Project', Operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Docket Number 'CP19-12', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2020-04-07, Cost $5M, Capacity +75 MMcf/d, Diameter 24in, States AL/MS/LA, Notes 'New delivery point to Entergy Louisiana; bidirectional flow on mainline'. Same docket, same capacity figure, same counterparty (Entergy Louisiana) in both -- this is not a GEM-only entity. NOTE ON THE WIKI'S OWN CITATION POOL: the harvested pool for this wiki page (9 citations) is the whole-system FGT reference list, not East-Louisiana-specific -- none of the 9 harvested URLs name this specific project (the closest, 'oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491', is a DIFFERENT pipeline id than the East Louisiana Project page I located independently at oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/3290, which I could not verify live -- see Length note). I opened all 9 harvested citations' URLs list and confirmed none of them individually names 'East Louisiana' -- both refs I am staging come from open-web search, not the harvest pool. CLASSIFICATION: correctly coded as part of FGT's interstate natural-gas transmission mainline system (NGA section 7(c)/blanket-certificate facility work), not a gathering/gathering-adjacent or processing line -- both sources describe 'natural gas mainline facilities'/'firm transportation service'. DUPLICATE check against the 37-PID Gulf Coast roster: 'East Louisiana' is one of 14 explicitly-named, individually FERC-docketed FGT expansion phases in this roster (Phase IV/V/VI/VII/VIII, East Leg, Western Division, Jacksonville, Sanford, Putnam, Turkey Point, Alabama Power, AE Cooperative, Mobile Bay, East Louisiana, South Alabama, Southwest Alabama) -- CP19-12 is a docket distinct from every other FGT docket found in the EIA workbook (see cross_row_leads, which independently matches 16 of the other 16 FGT roster rows to their own distinct EIA project rows/dockets). Not a duplicate of any sibling row.

Status is inferable from context, not a literal string match (per url_verifier guidance). EIA's tracker marks the project 'Completed' as of 2020-04-07 and it is coded as adding permanent firm-transportation capacity to FGT's mainline (not a temporary/test facility). Energy Transfer's current (2026) FGT informational-postings portal (fgtmessenger.energytransfer.com/ipost/main/index?asset=FGT), a live EBB with current capacity/nomination postings, confirms the FGT system this facility belongs to is presently in active commercial operation. Two independent origins (US government tracker vs. current operator posting system).

Trivially confirmed: both the FERC Federal Register notice ('natural gas mainline facilities...firm transportation service') and EIA's tracker (a row in EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' table) describe this as a natural gas project.

Not changing LengthKnown=0; flagging for a human to spot-check FERC eLibrary accession 20181107-5128 (FGT's actual CP19-12 prior-notice filing) directly if the ~1,000 ft detail needs resolving.

validity.recommendation: keep Diameter=24 as sourced, but note the tension with the 'no-new-pipe -> blank diameter' convention for the orchestrator's awareness
validity.researcher_notes: Diameter=24in is stated explicitly and specifically for this exact docket (CP19-12) by EIA's tracker ('Pipeline Diameter (Inches): 24'). This is currently a SINGLE source for the diameter figure itself -- the FERC Federal Register notice text I read does not restate a pipe diameter (expected: it is a prior-notice summary, not a full certificate order with engineering detail). Searched for a second source (FERC eLibrary full docket record, PHMSA NPMS data for FGT's mainline diameter at this milepost) and found none stating an explicit diameter for this specific facility beyond EIA. Tension worth flagging: the project convention is 'expansion with no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0, Diameter=blank', and this project has LengthKnown=0 (confirmed above), which would normally argue for blanking Diameter too. However EIA's own record explicitly and specifically states Diameter=24 for THIS docket despite ALSO recording Miles=blank -- i.e. EIA's methodology evidently records the diameter of the existing mainline pipe being modified/tied into, not just diameter-of-new-pipe. 24in is also consistent with the diameter of several sibling FGT segments in this same corridor (P2627 Mobile Bay Lateral=24in, P4033 Turkey Point=24in, P4036 Phase V Stage 3=24in -- see cross_row_leads), so it is plausible and not an outlier. Recommend keeping the sourced value rather than blanking on convention alone, since it is independently, specifically confirmed for this docket -- but flagging rather than silently applying the general rule.
